newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Defiant Berisha to call election, starts campaign.
newsitem.headline: Defiant Berisha to call election, starts campaign.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha defiantly launched his election campaign on Wednesday, saying he would call a poll for June 29 despite threats by other political parties to boycott the vote.
"I started the electoral campaign here and I will finish it here," Berisha told a crowd of supporters in this town some 50 kms (30 miles) to the southwest of Tirana.
"The day of June 29 will be the deepest victory of Albanian democracy," he added.

Early elections are seen as a key part of international efforts to stop Albania sliding back into the chaos of February and March, when rioting broke out across the country after pyramid investment schemes collapsed.

But other parties of a government of national unity, formed amid the March riots, have said they will not stand in the elections if they are held under a law which Berisha's Democratic Party pushed through parliament on Tuesday.
The new crisis forced European envoy Franz Vranitzky into a decision to rush back to Tirana on Thursday to defuse the situation.
Berisha insisted he would later dissolve parliament and said today marked the start of his campaign.

"Today in the afternoon I will decree the election day and will dissolve the parliament, which you elected (last year) with your free vote, the martyr parliament of the rebellion and we will elect a more powerful and wiser parliament," he said.
Many policemen and guards in civilian clothes armed with Kalashnikovs lined the square where Berisha spoke while other guards watched with binoculars from the tops of buildings.
Many in the south of the country, which was the epicentre of the violence, blame Berisha for the collapse of the schemes, in which hundreds of thousands lost money.
But the north of the country is seen as a stronghold for the Democrats and the president.
A small crowd waved blue Democratic Party flags and chanted "Berisha president" and "Down with communism" although several hundred people nearby seemed to be listening impassively.
Berisha, in his usual rich rhetorical style, said the elections would see his Democrats triumph again.
"We go to the elections sure that we will win and have one of the biggest victories for democracy," he said.
